items_missed: 1_set_agenda: No 'how are you today,' no agenda statement (what we'd cover / how long it'd take), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
2_probe: No probing for special considerations (narrow hallways/tight turns), box count, storage stops, additional stops, moving stressors, or destination floor/stairs.

3_pricing: No No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no disassembly/reassembly mention; the 'what's included' pitch covered taxes/insurance/CC fees but skipped gas, truck, wrap pads, bands, and tools.
4_clock: No 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute proration mentioned, no sense-check ('does that make sense?') after explaining the clock.

5_estimate: No equivalents used (school bus reference), no walk-distance or assembly/disassembly variables named, didn't tie the caller's oversized/fragile item into the time estimate, number of trucks not stated.
6_save_your_ass: Prep speech never given at all — no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill' framing.
7_quote_booking: Never said 'reply with any corrections' to verify the email details, never gave branch hours or how to reach the office.
8_politeness: Never used the customer's actual name (Glen/Gwynn) once — relied on 'ma'am' the whole call.
9_bonus: No rapport-building or humor, no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60c/lb baseline), no budget-conscious framing offered.
top_strength: Cameron's pricing walkthrough was clear and transparent, breaking the $340 combined trip fee and $208/hr rate down step by step, and he stayed unruffled when the caller corrected the home's square footage mid-call ('No problem... definitely work with that') without losing his place in the quote.
coaching_note: Cameron, the pricing breakdown was genuinely well done - that's the hardest part of the call and you handled it cleanly. But this call is missing nearly every differentiator we have: no Save Your Ass prep speech, no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee. Those aren't extras - they're what makes our quote feel different from a generic number, and skipping all four in one call is a real gap. Also use the customer's name a few times instead of just 'ma'am' - you had it, you just never used it. Add a quick agenda statement up front ('I'll grab some details then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes, sound good?') so the caller knows what to expect.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient throughout (especially when the caller corrected herself on square footage), but transactional word choice with no humor or rapport-building moments.
